messages.author: 8ee41a379d8797bf
messages.subject: Error 457
parts:
Hi, 
I am using Distance 6.2 Release 1. In some models I get this error:
Initializing 
Making data files 
Making Data Selection Queries 
Found selection criterion: {SELECT * FROM [lyrObservation] WHERE Species ='Gme' AND Obs_n='ok' AND [Perp distance]>=0} 
Found selection criterion: {SELECT * FROM [lyrLine transect] WHERE Strata IN ('S1','S2','S3','S4','S5')} 
** Error: Unexpected error **
 Error Source: DataFileMaker.MakeObsQuery
 Internal Error number: 457.
 Internal Error description: "This key is already associated with an element of this collection".

but the same exact filter with other models everything goes fine. Anyone knows what this problem is and how to solve it?
Thanks
 Ana

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Error 457
parts:
Anna

This error has been discussed a couple of times on this list.  In previous situations, analysts were trying to analyse single observer-collected data with the MRDS engine (intended to analyse double observer data).  The error arose regarding the existence of a field named "Observer" in the data and what that field contains.

Have a look at this discussion on the list from 2014:  https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/distance-sampling/This$20key$20is$20already$20associated$20with$20an$20element$20of$20this$20collection/distance-sampling/O5rgXC00fUM/3QBgUwOwa9gJ

You say this query works on some analyses and not others; are the ones for which it fails MRDS-based?  If so, make sure the "Observer" field is used as expected by MRDS.

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Error 457
parts:
Ana

I suspect the error is not coming about as a result of your data filter, but rather as a result of your use of the "special" Detected field (that you have renamed Seen) being text rather than numeric.

Note this passage from the Users Guide:

Double observer data has two fields that can be used in conjunction with the data selection options in the Data Filter to achieve the desired analysis. The two fields are observer (which is 1 for the first observer and 2 for the second) and detected (which is 1 if the animal was detected by that observer and 0 if not; note that the actual field names may be different from this).

The passage notes that you can change the field names, but there in no indication you can change the field contents (or type).

My advice is to change your fields Y=>1, N=>0 and specify the field is of type integer when imported.

You say this query works on some analyses and not others; are the ones for which it fails MRDS-based?  If so, make sure the "Observer" field is used as expected by MRDS.
